State ------ Appellant

Balai Chandra Sarker ------ Condemned-accused
full_judgment: 10. Even being frightened of the torture by police in our country one may abscond, but abscondance cannot be presumption or inference of guilt without any supporting evidence or conclusive circumstance. From the conduct of a person for absconding after commission of the offence may sometimes be evidence to show that he was concerned with the offence. But it is usually a very small item in the evidence on which a conviction can be based (Section 8 of the Evidence Act) Mansur Elahi vs. State PLD 1965 (Lah) 656, Crown vs. Fateh Mohammed 35 PLR, 740. In this case the investigation should have been more prompt and more truthful. It is very shocking that in our country the police are very callous and their role is not up to the mark and necessity, to bring the culprit to book to help the court in coming to the legal conclusion. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the evidence on record, the discussions made above and the legal principles referred to we are satisfied that the prosecution could not prove the allegation of killing of deceased Beauty Rani Sarker by her husband Balai Chandra Sarker, the condemned accused beyond all reasonable doubt and therefore, to convict him under section 302 of the Penal Code and awarding capital sentence as has been done by the learned Sessions Judge is not free from infirmity and not sustainable in law.
